skill.name: resolving-merge-conflicts
skill.description: Guides agents through resolving active Git merge and rebase conflicts while preserving source intent and validating the result.
skill.summary: Resolve Git conflicts by tracing intent, reconciling changes, and running project checks.
skill.author: mattpocock

security_audit.summary: The static alert is a false positive because line 10 uses Markdown backticks around a Git option, not Ruby or shell execution. No prompt injection or data-exfiltration intent was found. However, unconditional instructions to never abort and to stage everything can capture unrelated changes or remove a safe recovery option.

remediation.issue: The workflow requires resolution, broad staging, and a commit without checking for unrelated work or requesting confirmation.
remediation.suggestion: Require a clean worktree check and user confirmation before staging or committing. Permit aborting when intent is unclear or recovery is safer.

content.value_statement: Merge and rebase conflicts often hide competing design intentions. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through research, resolution, validation, and completion.
actual_capabilities: Inspects the active merge or rebase state, Git history, and conflicting files.
Traces each conflicting change through commits, pull requests, issues, and tickets.
Resolves conflict hunks while preserving compatible intent and documenting necessary trade-offs.
Discovers and runs project checks such as type checking, tests, and formatting.
Stages resolved files, completes the merge commit, or continues the rebase sequence.
limitations: Requires repository access and an active merge or rebase conflict.
Cannot guarantee the intended result when commits and project records lack context.
Does not provide project-specific commands for checks or conflict resolution.
Broad staging can include unrelated changes unless the worktree and staged diff are reviewed.

use_cases.title: Complete a Feature Merge
use_cases.description: Reconcile a feature branch with recent mainline changes while preserving both documented intentions.

use_cases.title: Recover a Rebase
use_cases.description: Resolve conflicts across several rebased commits and verify each continuation against project checks.

use_cases.title: Review an Automated Resolution
use_cases.description: Trace conflict decisions to commits and tickets before accepting an agent-generated integration.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect the Conflict
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect the active Git merge or rebase. List conflicting files, summarize each side, and identify the next safe action. Do not modify files yet.

prompt_templates.title: Resolve One File
prompt_templates.prompt: Resolve the conflicts in [file]. Use commit history to explain both intentions, preserve compatible behavior, and report every trade-off before staging.
prompt_templates.scenario: Focused resolution of one conflicting file

prompt_templates.title: Validate the Integration
prompt_templates.prompt: Review all resolved files, discover project checks, and run relevant type checks, tests, and formatting. Report failures caused by the integration.

prompt_templates.title: Complete a Complex Rebase
prompt_templates.prompt: Resolve the active rebase across remaining commits. Research each conflict, preserve intended behavior, validate each step, and request confirmation before staging or continuing.

output_examples.input: Inspect my active merge and explain the conflict before changing files.
output: Two files are conflicted: the account service and its tests.
One branch adds validation, while the other changes the persistence workflow.
Both intentions can be preserved by validating before the updated persistence call.

output_examples.input: Resolve the rebase and report validation results.
output: The conflicting API rename was applied to the rebased feature logic.
The related tests were updated without adding new behavior.
Type checking and tests passed. Formatting changed one resolved file.

output_examples.input: Explain an incompatible conflict and recommend a resolution.
output_examples.output: The branches define different retry limits for the same operation. The release ticket supports the lower limit, so the higher limit should be rejected.

best_practices: Inspect status, history, commits, and project records before editing conflict markers.
Keep unrelated worktree changes separate from the merge or rebase resolution.
Review the staged diff and run relevant checks before committing or continuing.
anti_patterns: Resolve conflicts from nearby code alone without checking commit or ticket intent.
Invent new behavior while combining incompatible changes.
Stage the entire working tree without reviewing unrelated or sensitive files.

faq.question: Does this skill resolve both merge and rebase conflicts?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers active merges and rebases, including repeated conflict resolution while continuing a multi-commit rebase.

faq.question: Will it choose one side automatically?
faq.answer: No. It first researches each change and preserves both intentions when they are compatible.

faq.question: What context does it inspect?
faq.answer: It can inspect Git history, commit messages, pull requests, issues, tickets, and conflicting files when those sources are available.

faq.question: Does it run project checks?
faq.answer: Yes. It directs the agent to discover and run relevant type checks, tests, and formatting.

faq.question: Can it guarantee a correct resolution?
faq.answer: No. Correctness depends on available context, accurate project records, and meaningful automated checks.

faq.question: Should it stage and commit without review?
faq.answer: No. Review the worktree and staged diff, then confirm the intended changes before committing or continuing a rebase.
